applicability.rationale: The bundle targets the owned lifecycle R path at exact 2eb and the frozen fixed-origin candidate already source-reviewed for Linux-only integration.

confidence.rationale: All four exact script bytes, AST syntax, builder/prepare field compatibility, every hard-coded candidate/peer/archive source digest, current R state, candidate full-index patch, source receipt fields and prior immutable-source closure checks were inspected read-only.

impact.rationale: The admitted workflow stages 14 shared source paths, LIVE, ten evidence archives and a generated integration record, then creates and pushes a lifecycle development-branch commit. A defect could affect shared Linux recovery behavior or publish incorrect audit evidence, although production, main and Registry remain outside scope.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A substituted prepare or integrator could weaken admission or stage a different set after the review.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The reviewed prepare, integrator, replay helper and input builder must be the exact files used for one integration.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The builder verifies supplied prepare and integrator SHA values, hard-pins the replay helper, and this review pins the builder; prepare verifies itself and the integrator again, while the integrator verifies itself before any repository stage or commit.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A valid unrelated JSON must not be accepted under any fixed-origin evidence filename.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The four new archive destinations must contain exactly the selected candidate receipt, implementation peer, policy peer and coordinator review.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The builder fixes candidate and peer sources and emits an independently supplied coordinator pin. Prepare reconstructs the expected role map, requires exact implementation/policy roles and basenames, hashes every pin, and requires each NEW4 source path and SHA to equal its selected origin.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A stale receipt name/count, alternate manifest, divergent working-tree diff or peer for another patch must stop.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The candidate receipt, manifest, patch, afterimages and both peer reviews must all describe one exact immutable 14-path change.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Prepare requires candidate manifest/patch/receipt pins, strict receipt schema/count/name/bytes/SHA, exact manifest schema/base/tree/14 unique rows/mode/LF/hash/blob data, byte-equal full-index patch, and both peer patch objects' sourceType/base/SHA/14-file set.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Dropping, replacing or adding a historical archive, or staging unrelated dirty data, must fail.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Exactly six named preexisting untracked archives and LIVE must be preserved while exactly four new archives are added.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Builder requires the actual six-name untracked set and captures exact UTF-8 working bytes; prepare requires exact six working copies, exact total ten destinations, semantic equality to each historical source, exact stage/finalize dirty sets and immutable-base candidate preimages.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: R working tree and resulting commit

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Count-preserving path substitutions, privacy drift, broader contract changes or unrelated kernel edits must fail.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The integrated source must retain exact continuous, profile, contract, policy, privacy, kernel and normal-name closures.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Finalization derives exact delivery/FMT ordering, base CAPACITY plus exact three and old FULL extras, unchanged Go args, schema-v2 plus two contract fields, policy-only delivery33, byte-identical private functions, reversible six kernel wrappers, HTTP31 and normal 688 hash from immutable 2eb.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: continuous recovery and capacity-profile source contracts

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A source-only pass could otherwise be mistaken for compiled or real 31-request recovery acceptance.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Source integration must not be represented as exact-head Linux or production acceptance.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Plan/evidence explicitly keep actualNewRuntimeAccepted, performanceBenefitProven, production, mainMerged, registryPublished, fullDiagnosticTimeoutResolved and fullSystemComplete false; Linux/runtime evidence remains a separate next gate.

protectiveFactors: The four-file bundle is pinned by exact SHA256; prepare and integrator verify their configured bytes, the replay helper has a fixed hash, and the builder verifies its supplied prepare/integrator hashes before output.
The builder pins four candidate artifacts, two role-distinct peer receipts and six historical source receipts, and writes one fixed O_EXCL+fsync input only after all checks.
NEW4 sources are mapped exactly to candidate receipt, implementation peer, policy peer and independently supplied coordinator-review pin; archive path and SHA must match the selected origin.
The source receipt now requires exact schema, changed count, manifest/patch names, byte counts and hashes in addition to base commit/tree.
The candidate full-index binary diff remains byte-identical to patch c115323d... and all prior profile, continuous, privacy, kernel reversal and normal-688 guards remain.

recoverability.rationale: No migration or production write is involved. The development commit can be reverted, but CPU replay occurs after the local commit and a pushed failure requires a controlled branch revert while preserving LIVE and the six original evidence files.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The integration touches architecture-specific Linux process observation and public evidence schemas, and exact-head Go evidence must follow integration. The source admission path now has exact pins, role-bound archives, strict receipt fields and immutable-base derivations, with no remaining deterministic source defect found.

regressionProtection.rationale: The source contract protects the exact four orchestration files, 14-path patch, manifest rows, two peer patch identities, six existing and four new role-bound archives, profile/continuous/contract/policy closures and schedules 303 CPU checks plus final-head source replay. It deliberately does not claim exact-head Linux compilation, formatting or runtime acceptance before the single integration.

riskDrivers: The admitted patch changes shared Linux observation and serialized evidence contracts.
The integrator commits before running the post-commit CPU/source replay and pushes only after those checks.
Exact-head Linux Go, official formatting and real continuous runtime evidence must be obtained after integration.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without this candidate, the continuous recovery evidence cannot distinguish the required source-owned kill origins. The corrected orchestrator now admits that source without weakening the existing runtime or evidence gates.

unknowns.summary: The coordinator-review path/hash must be supplied from this retained v3 review when the builder is run; this is an operational input, not an unresolved source decision.
Exact integrated-head Linux formatting, compile/race and runtime acceptance remain the next rollout gate.
